name: hazel_weir_central_procedural_graph
description: Optimized Central Procedural Graph featuring continuous land scaling for 10 hands, Day 30 Town Shop arbitrage delivery, active plot fertilization dispatch, and zero-animal feed reserve liberation.

nodes.name: State & Balance Audit
nodes.description: Computes net available cash, shed fill percentage, wage liability, active shop contract demand, and oracle price drop signals across market commodities.

nodes.name: Midnight Wage Reserve Defense
nodes.description: Protects payroll for all active hired hands. Enforces dynamic cash reserve locks and triggers pre-midnight surplus liquidation to prevent the 0-hand bankruptcy cascade.

nodes.name: Town Shop Demand Arbitrage
nodes.description: Preemptively matches unlocked town shop demand surges and fulfills mature high-margin crops (Carrots, Tomatoes, Pumpkins, Strawberries) through Day 30 to capture 2.0x-3.5x contract price premiums.

nodes.name: Shed Headroom Relief
nodes.description: Prevents silent 100/100 harvest discards by clearing uncommitted low-margin inventory under strict price floors while protecting active animal feed, shop contracts, and executing Day 30 terminal liquidation.

nodes.name: Oracle Opponent Front-Run
nodes.description: Reads 96-step TTM forecast to dump sensitive commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) immediately before opponent market gluts collapse prices.

nodes.name: Capital Reinvestment & Yield Scaling
nodes.description: Reinvests surplus cash beyond wage reserves into workforce acceleration (10-hand rush), contiguous land expansion (up to 24 plots), commercial high-yield seeds, and fertilizer.

nodes.name: Routine Farm & Workforce Execution
nodes.description: Executes field routines with strict operational sequencing: harvest ready crops, immediate worker drop-offs, watering, fertilizing high-margin plots, livestock feeding, planting, and ground maintenance.

attributes.guidance: Cancel non-essential purchases (BUY_SEED, BUY_ANIMAL, BUY_LAND, redundant HIRE); schedule worker harvest drop-offs before hour 21; enforce emergency liquidation of non-feed, non-contract inventory at hour >= 20 to guarantee payroll.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell Wheat below dynamic livestock feed reserve (n_animals * 3 if n_animals > 0 else 0); do not rely on low-margin fertilizer sales to cover payroll deficits; never liquidate crops committed to active town shop delivery.

attributes.guidance: Allocate up to 3 market slots to deliver matching mature shed inventory directly to town shops for 2.0x-3.5x premium through Day 30; procure shop-demanded seeds (Carrots, Tomatoes, Pumpkins, Strawberries) through day 26 when surplus cash covers seed costs and wage buffers.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not commit seed capital if net cash falls below 1.25x midnight payroll reserve; do not purchase shop seeds after day 26 that cannot mature before day 30; do not purchase shop seeds if shed capacity exceeds 88%; never hold shop produce past contract expiration windows.

attributes.condition: shed_used + incoming_worker_inventory >= 82 or (day == 30 and hour >= 22 and shed_used > 0)
attributes.guidance: Evict pending non-urgent buy orders to free order slots; execute batch sales of unreserved, non-shop surplus holdings with price >= 0.70 * base_price; only relax floor to 0.45 * base_price if shed_used >= 95 to prevent discard drops. On day 30 hour >= 22, execute complete terminal liquidation of all remaining shed inventory.
attributes.pitfalls: Never fire-sell at sub-0.50 base price during transient shed spikes; never liquidate Wheat below livestock feed reserve (n_animals * 3 if n_animals > 0 else 0); never evict produce allocated for active town shop fulfillment.

attributes.guidance: Preempt lowest-margin open orders; execute rapid batch liquidations of vulnerable commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) while current market price remains favorable (> 0.75 * base_price) before opponent dumping collapses market prices.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not dump into already collapsed sub-0.50 base price markets unless shed overflow is imminent; do not front-run commodities committed to active town shop contracts.

attributes.condition: net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.35 + 250.0 and (hired_hands < 10 or uncultivated_plots <= 2 or has_fertilizer_deficit) and day <= 26
attributes.guidance: When surplus cash covers wage buffers: 1) Scale workforce to the 10-hand cap as top early priority; 2) Acquire contiguous land plots up to 24 plots through day 20 whenever uncultivated plots <= 2 to eliminate worker idle time; 3) Procure commercial seeds (Pumpkins, Tomatoes, Strawberries) and fertilizer to maximize per-plot yield throughput; 4) Transition seed purchases to fast-maturing crops after day 25 and halt all land/hand expansion after day 26.
attributes.pitfalls: Never allocate reinvestment capital if net cash after purchase drops below 1.30x midnight wage buffer; do not acquire land plots beyond 24 plots or that hands cannot consistently water; never buy slow-growing seeds (Pumpkins/Strawberries) after day 25 that cannot mature before day 30.

attributes.guidance: Dispatch active hands strictly by operational priority: 1) Harvest mature crops; 2) Drop off carried items at shed immediately; 3) Water dry crops; 4) Apply fertilizer to commercial high-margin plots (Pumpkins, Tomatoes, Strawberries); 5) Feed hungry livestock; 6) Plant commercial seeds; 7) Weed clearing and ground tilling. Ensure all carried inventory is deposited at shed by step 716 for terminal liquidation.
attributes.pitfalls: Never defer shed drop-offs when hands carry harvested produce; never prioritize weeding over harvesting, watering, or fertilizing; do not leave mature crops unharvested across multi-step windows; ensure hands never idle while unharvested crops or dry plots remain.
